supersedes: v1.2 is retained as a historical invalid replay because an eight-thread client pool back-pressured the planned 24-request arrival process. v1.3 uses one timed client per request, gates measured arrival slip, binds every raw response to the frozen workload, recomputes LongBench F1, uses twelve independent process blocks, and applies phase-and-action-homogeneous graph boundaries.
arm_order: balanced seeded Direct/Paged process order inside matched process blocks

replay.arrival_transform: Within each official contiguous trace window, divide every offset by the window span and multiply by 1.5 seconds. One independently timed client is created per request so completed HTTP calls cannot back-pressure admission. This preserves order and relative gaps subject to the preregistered arrival-slip gate but intentionally changes absolute rate.

quality.metric: official LongBench English QA token F1, maximum over reference answers

statistics.effect: 100 * (Paged-hybrid completed requests per second / Direct completed requests per second - 1)
statistics.confidence: matched-process-block cluster bootstrap 95% intervals for throughput effect and pooled request-P95 regression

claim_boundary: Passing supports functional equivalence and a 10% throughput/15% request-P95 operational noninferiority envelope for the forced production contiguous-layout Paged route across the full generated decode lifecycle on this model, GPU, two transformed public traces and six supported LongBench QA cases. It does not show custom fragmented-page K4 superiority, does not reproduce the public traces' absolute arrival rates or joint content-arrival distribution, and is not a full LongBench or LongBench-E leaderboard result.
